Additionally, the notes confirm that the sink cell flag is set to true or false, and the definition of a sink cell is a cell whose flag is still set (true) after the PN relation processing.

If the viewpoint is outside the mesh, discard the last entry (back-facing face where the ray enters the mesh) [S1].

The claim states that if the viewpoint is outside the mesh, the last entry (back-facing face where the ray enters the mesh) should be discarded. The evidence in Source [S1] explicitly states: '(If the viewpoint is outside the mesh, the PIX lists have an even number of entries, so the last entry on the PIX list, the face through which the ray enters the mesh for the first time, is also not used.)' This confirms that the last entry is indeed not used (discarded) in this specific scenario.

Identify pairs where the first entry refers to a front-facing face and the second refers to a back-facing face [S1].

The evidence explicitly states that 'Except for the first and last entries on a PIX list, consecutive entries alternate between referring to a front-facing face of a cell and a back-facing face of another cell.' It further defines these pairs as pseudoneighbors (PNs), where the cell contributing the back-facing face is the 'occluding PN' and the other is the 'occluded PN'. The notes also mention identifying 'consecutive entries on a PIX list... as front-facing/back-facing pairs.' Thus, the evidence supports the claim that the algorithm identifies pairs where the first entry refers to a front-facing face and the second refers to a back-facing face (within the context of the alternating sequence described).
